strings.name: John Clauser
strings.summary: Born in California, Clauser studied physics at Caltech and Columbia. He helped formulate the CHSH inequality in 1969 and conducted entangled-photon experiments with Stuart Freedman that violated Bell inequalities, supporting tests of quantum theory and quantum information. He shared the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics with Aspect and Zeilinger. His later public denial of a climate crisis drew scientific criticism; those views do not represent climate-science consensus and are not validated by a quantum-research prize.

strings.influence.rationale: Advanced tests of quantum theory through Bell-inequality experiments, providing an experimental foundation for quantum entanglement and quantum information research.

strings.highlights.h1.title: Testing quantum theory
strings.highlights.h1.text: Conducted early Bell-inequality experiments with Freedman, providing evidence for entangled correlations.
strings.highlights.h2.title: CHSH and quantum information
strings.highlights.h2.text: Helped formulate experimentally testable inequalities, influencing quantum foundations and information science.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Controversial climate statements
strings.timeline.t1.text: Publicly denied a climate crisis; climate researchers and fact-checkers identified conflicts with evidence and consensus.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Sharing the Nobel Prize in Physics
strings.timeline.t2.text: Recognized with Alain Aspect and Anton Zeilinger for entangled-photon experiments and related work.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Sharing the Wolf Prize in Physics
strings.timeline.t3.text: Recognized with Aspect and Zeilinger for experimental contributions to quantum foundations.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Clauser–Horne inequality
strings.timeline.t4.text: Developed an experimental framework for testing local theories with Michael Horne.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Entangled-photon experiment
strings.timeline.t5.text: Observed Bell-inequality violations with Freedman, consistent with quantum predictions.
strings.timeline.t6.title: CHSH inequality
strings.timeline.t6.text: Developed an experimentally testable Bell-type inequality with Horne, Shimony and Holt.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Columbia doctorate
strings.timeline.t7.text: Earned a physics doctorate and began Berkeley research, later pursuing quantum foundations experiments.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Caltech bachelor’s degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed undergraduate physics before graduate study at Columbia.
